Hi Phil,

I'm very thankful for your help and quite sorry to bother you again!

As you suggested, I'm currently trying to work with the customNextItem()-Function in order to archive a min_items criteria for each factor.
To do that I'm creating a counter object (data frame with rows = nfact) that is increased by the customNextItem() by +1 for the specific factor each time an item is chosen. I then can break the MCAT by returning NA, if !any(counter < min_items). This is realized through an (external/additional) object in my global environment, which is deleted and reestablished after every person.

Unfortunately, this solution is merely a work-around and has at least to flaws: 1. It is prone to error when the external counter is not correctly deleted and reestablished for a new person and 2. I cannot directly access the counter through the person object during or after MCAT since it's not connected to each other (meaning the counter is not bound to a specific person). It would be nice to have a more robust solution as well as the possibility to access the counter post-CAT for evaluation.

Hence my new question: Do you know any possibility to add and save this counter as a field in the person-object? I haven't yet found a possibility to add a field to an instance of a reference class object by the customNextItem function. Or maybe you know a more elegant solution to my problem other than working with an additional object in the global environment?

Last question: You told me MCAT is not supporting termination based on single factor criteria like min_items for each dimension. Yet with extract.mirtCAT(x = design, what = "met_SEM") I get a vector with logical values for each factor. So unlike min_items, min_SEM is supported for MCAT? What about delta_thetas?

Thank you very much in advance and best wishes!
Nick

messages.subject: Re: Thetas with 'inf' values
messages.subject_clean: Thetas with 'inf' values
messages.body_plain:
I assume you're estimating the theta's using the ML criteria, which is problematic in that a unique mode is often not found with extreme response patterns (only gets worse with multiple dimensions, as the problem becomes conditional on the trait too). The value |20| is a maximum allowed by the iterative algorithms because even though a unique mode could exist, sometimes they do not due to the combination of response functions and extremeness of the observation. Hence, I would take the values 20 to mean the algorithm failed to converge for that response pattern (you should have seen warning messages). You might want to use the MAP criteria instead as it includes the density of the latent trait in the estimation criteria. HTH.

Phil

I wanted to assess three versions of a CRT cognitive measure, the original 3-item measure and two longer versions - an 8-item version and 11-item version applying item response theory analyses (a two-parameter logistic model), to see whether the longer versions are appropriate for participants with both lower and higher levels of the latent trait.
All the items are binary with no missing values.
Sample size is 448.

#importing data
df.NA.zaCRT3 <- read_csv("data_N448.csv")
df.NA.zaCRT3 <- df.NA.zaCRT3[,-1]

psych::describe(df.NA.zaCRT3)
#Checking for missing values -> none are missing
colSums(is.na <http://is.na>(df.NA.zaCRT3))

#selecting items and forming 3 data frames:
podaci.CRT.rec <- as.data.frame(dplyr::select(df.NA.zaCRT3, CRT1:CRT11)) #data frame with all the 11 items
podaci.CRT8.rec <- as.data.frame(dplyr::select(df.NA.zaCRT3, CRT1:CRT3, CRT5:CRT8,CRT11)) #data frame with 8 items
podaci.CRT3.rec <- as.data.frame(dplyr::select(df.NA.zaCRT3, CRT1:CRT3)) # df s prve3 CRT #data frame with 3 original items

##------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#11-items 2PL model:
fit.crt11.2pl <- mirt(podaci.CRT.rec, model = 1, calcNull = T,  SE = T)

#Model fit:
round(M2(fit.crt11.2pl, na.rm = T), 3)

> Thanks so much for this helpful package. I have a question about fscores when using mixture IRT (e.g., using multipleGroup and dentype = "mixture-4").

> Using the command "fscores", is the default a weighted EAP score (weighted by the probability of class membership)?

Correct.

> Also, how is the SE calculated for the fscores - is it a weighted SE or more complicated?

No particularly, it's still the posterior standard deviation of the trait estimates, however the information about the SD is treated as a composite as well in the same way (the math to find the EAP is pretty much the same as for the posterior SD that substitutes the EAP estimate into the equation). messages.body_plain:
dear Balazs,

It is my understanding that in IRT, item and ability parameters are invariant, i.e. ability estimates are not test dependent and item parameters are not group dependent. If the estimation of theta is also dependent on group membership, you might have Different Item Functioning (DIF) - you don't want DIF. If an item shows DIF then persons with the same trait level do not have the same probability to endorse that item.

Cheers, Guido
